newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Portugal's Sampaio begins Mozambique visit.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Sampaio begins Mozambique visit.

text.p: Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio arrived in Mozambique on Monday for a week-long state visit, his first official trip to Africa since he took office in March last year.
A few hours after his arrival Sampaio began talks with Mozambican President Joaquim Chissano on cooperation between the two countries.
Mozambique fought a 10-year war for independence from Portugal until 1975. A civil war then erupted between the ruling Frelimo government and Renamo rebels who signed a peace agreement in 1992.
Sampaio, a socialist, was an opponent of the Portuguese colonial government and a supporter of the African independence movement.
He is scheduled to address the parliament and visit Portuguese-run enterprises in the provinces of Nampula, Sofala, Tete and Zambezia. He is accompanied by 36 businessmen.

Later Sampaio will tour the giant Cahora Bassa hydro-electric project built by the Portuguese in colonial times, but which was later damaged by the South African army during cross-border raids against anti-apartheid activists living in Mozambique.
The plant is due to be relaunched this year and will supply electricity to South Africa.
Statistics in 1993 show Portugal was the main destination for exports from Mozambique.
